description: github.com/wakeshift/wakeshift-go: wake the conversation that started the work when it finishes. Your MCP server's tools subscribe the calling conversation to your app's events, and Wakeshift wakes it (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ChatGPT and others) when you emit. Built on the official Go MCP SDK, with an adapter for mark3labs/mcp-go.
rules: Create the client with wakeshift.New(), which reads WAKESHIFT_KEY and does no I/O; without a key it's disabled and every call still works. Never hard-code the key or commit it.
Define every event with wakeshift.DefineEvent at startup, before calling wake.Attach. Text is optional.

An event with neither Personal, Authorize nor Public can be subscribed only by your own tools: keep that default for IDs your tool mints, use Personal for per-user things, Authorize for shared resources, and Public only for streams anyone may watch.

Register tools that subscribe with wakeshift.AddTool(attached, tool, handler, wakeshift.Subscribes(events...)); the handler is go-sdk's with the *wakeshift.ToolCall after ctx, and the input type is your own, with no Wakeshift fields.
Subscribe with event.Subscribe(ctx, call, args, wakeshift.Once()) before starting the work; use wakeshift.Replay(d) when the job's ID exists only after it started.
When the caller names a resource, check they can see it before Subscribe; call.User is Wakeshift's view, not your authorization.
Put attached.Handler in front of the MCP endpoint's HTTP handler, after its authentication; for a server built per request, use wake.Handler(next, opts).
Tools registered with srv.AddTool or a catalog go in AttachOptions.Wrap and find their call with wakeshift.ToolCallFrom(ctx).

Identify gets each request's ctx and wakeshift.Request (r.Token is the verified token); set RequireUser when the server requires sign-in. Authorize returns (bool, error) and never decides on Subscriber.Client or Native.
Pass wakeshift.WithID(deliveryID) to Emit when the source may retry; take personal recipients (wakeshift.To) from your own records, never from who's subscribed.
BuiltinTools: wakeshift.BuiltinTools{Wait: true} turns on wakeshift_wait; give the endpoint a write timeout of 30 seconds or more.
Check errors with wakeshift.IsCode(err, wakeshift.CodeX); never lowercase a case-sensitive ID: use wakeshift.EncodeArgValue.
Never log call.Session(), tokens or tool arguments; use wakeshift.RedactSecrets on text you log.
Write event descriptions as plain statements of what happened, not instructions to the agent.
